To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the most frequently-mentioned antonym-pairs of “up” and “down” verbs were identified by people; (b) the antonym pairs were identified in a way that was similar to their distribution in the corpus; and (c) the similarity of antonym pairs was correlated with the proportion of people that identified them as antonyms.

(i) the most frequently identified antonyms of the “UP and DOWN verbs” are those that have the most similar argument distributions, (ii) 87% of antonyms identified by people are either the most or second-most similar antonym pairs in the corpus and (iii) the cosine similarity of the argument-distributions correlates moderately (r = 31) with the proportions of people who identified the antonyms as opposites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: To what extent can we predict the antonyms of “UP and DOWN verbs” from a corpus analysis of their argument-distributions?
whether the antonymic relationships identified in a psychological study of the UP and Down metaphors can be predicted from a computational analysis of argument-distributions in our financial corpus.
the question of whether the distribution of arguments for a verb can be used to identify antonyms for that verb.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
“The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 0.2% on Tuesday”.
the market was up on the day and the FTSE was up 0.3 per cent, or up 10 points.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the distributional approach is a useful one for identifying the metaphoric antonyms of “UP” and “DOWN” verbs.
the antonym-pairs identified in our experiments were not predicted by the cosine similarity of the argument-distributions in our data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
distributional analyses can be a valuable tool for identifying metaphoric antonyms.
we are able to predict antonym-pairs from a corpus-based analysis of the argument-distributions of UP and DOWN verbs in a corpus of financial articles.
distributional approaches to meaning can be used to derive metaphoric opposites from corpora.
